claim: A Nature Communications paper published 2026-10-14 reports time-defined mechanically induced nucleation and a dimensionless model for crystallization across selected solution-processed perovskites, an organic semiconductor, and NaH2PO4. Selected FET demonstrations report improved mobility with controlled morphology; product-scale outcomes are not demonstrated.
whatChanged: New version-of-record paper links timed induced nucleation, morphology regimes, and domain-growth modeling across selected materials.
whyNow: Primary article, supplementary movies, and source-data links are newly available; computational reproduction is cheaper than immediate lab work.
readiness: Peer-reviewed laboratory study; exact-method independent replication and manufacturing-scale performance not established.
falsifier: A blinded independent reanalysis or protocol-matched replication fails to reproduce normalized growth curves or morphology windows on held-out conditions, or the mobility advantage disappears under device/contact-resistance controls.
firstUnsupportedArrow: Reported model and selected FET outcomes → independent replication → robust large-area manufacturing → improved product yield and economics.
omissions: Model scope depends on evaporation-governed concentration change and mass-transfer-limited growth.
Manual ROI and tunable image-processing thresholds require frozen, sensitivity-tested reanalysis.
A laboratory mobility gain is not product efficiency, stability, yield, or cost evidence.
Broad crystallization-control prior art exists; novelty and freedom to operate are unassessed.
No independent replication of the exact TDIN model found in the bounded search.
rivalHypotheses: Timed nucleation thresholds causally drive the morphology regimes.
The apparent universality is limited to evaporation- and diffusion-controlled systems.
Scratching changes wetting, thickness, defects, or evaporation beyond the proposed mechanism.
Device geometry, contact resistance, or image-analysis choices partly explain mobility differences.
crossDomainOpportunity: Open-source pipeline for source tables and microscopy movies, fixed segmentation, dimensionless-model fitting, and process sensitivity; any paid service remains speculative.
consequenceOwner: Thin-film laboratory if later replication is justified
nextBoundedMachineMove: Retrieve and hash source files through an approved route; freeze ROI/threshold rules; reproduce growth curves and fit statistics; test held-out conditions. No experiment, purchase, contact, publication, or deployment.
priorFindingOrLedger: UNKNOWN; bounded default-branch and PR-title searches found no matching candidate, but all-history search was not exhaustive.
